title: solo trial quicksheet - maya
content:
Quick personal sheet to track a few one-off inference trials. Intentionally messy — for my memory and quick comparisons.

Header: Date | Exp ID | Model | Variant | Prompt tag | Batch | SeqLen | Tokens/req | Avg Lat (ms) | P95 Lat (ms) | Est cost /1k toks | Notes
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2026-02-28 | EXP-53 | redwood-vicuna-7b-q4 | v2-short-context | prompt-A | 8 | 512 | 780 | 120 | 260 | $0.42 | memory spikes after ~300 reqs, GC visible; try batch 6 next
2026-03-03 | EXP-56 | redwood-vicuna-7b-q4 | v2-long-context | prompt-B | 4 | 1024 | 1550 | 210 | 380 | $0.48 | stable but higher tail lat; p95 driven by tail tokens + KV cache miss
2026-03-05 | EXP-58 | open-codex-13b-fp16 | prompt-tuned-0 | prompt-C | 2 | 256 | 410 | 340 | 720 | $1.15 | amazing quality, cost too high for product; note: try int8 quant next run
2026-03-09 | EXP-61 | redwood-llm-3b-8bit | baseline | prompt-A | 12 | 256 | 290 | 95 | 180 | $0.21 | best cost/lat so far; occasional completion truncation on long replies

Quick calculations (scratch):
- tokens_per_second ~= 1000 / avg_lat_ms * tokens_req ??? (rough heuristic)
- cost_per_token estimate used above: 
   * EXP-61: observed cost $0.061 per req for 290 tokens -> ~0.00021 $/token -> $0.21 per 1k tokens (rounded)
   * EXP-58: $0.47 per req for 410 tokens -> ~0.00115 $/token -> $1.15 per 1k
- Use these for quick product-level cost back-of-envelope. Not accurate accounting for batching inefficiencies.

Things I want to remember / TODOs:
- [ ] Run EXP-53 with batch=6 and note memory behavior; add perf counters (nvprof) the next run.
- [ ] Try static KV cache warmup step for EXP-56 to reduce p95.
- [ ] Re-run EXP-58 with int8 quant and measure quality delta (create separate sheet for quality evals)
- [ ] Add a cheap unit test harness to reproduce the truncation seen in EXP-61.

Open questions / quick notes:
- Why does batch increase sometimes reduce tail latency and sometimes increase it? hypoth: GC/allocator fragmentation + kernel scheduling interplay on multi-tenant nodes.
- Is there a simple heuristic to pick batch size by seqLen distribution? I should try batch ~ (max_seq / 64) as a guess.

Links to quick refs:
- ticket JIRA-ML-412: perf regression after kernel update (linked above)
- PR 889: small runtime change that may affect allocator behavior

Rough meeting notes snippet (copied here so I can find later):
- 2026-03-11 quick sync w/ Liam: he suggested measuring mem-bandwidth per model + simple sampling of p95 across time windows. Good idea.
- Also suggested automating the cheap KV-warmup step.

End of sheet — will split into formal tracking doc if any of these experiments become longer-running or need to be shared.
